title: First-commit rituals and smoke-loop manifesto
body:
Purpose:
This doc collects lightweight, repeatable rituals for the very first commit and the accompanying smoke-loop that the SDK team (and integrators) can run in ~10–15 minutes. The aim is pragmatic: reduce friction for new contributors and CI, catch obvious regressions early, and surface telemetry so product and infra teams can iterate on onboarding metrics.

Why this matters (short):
- First-commit is a fragile moment: build failures, missing credentials, or flaky tests derail momentum.
- A tiny, opinionated ritual lowers cognitive load for engineers and customer engineers working with the SDK.
- The smoke-loop is the quick safety net we run before opening PRs or demoing a sampleapp.

What this doc is not: a full CI spec or exhaustive test plan. It is a lightweight manual that can be automated later (and should be).

High-level ritual (first-commit):
1) Local preflight (5 minutes)
   - git clone + checkout branch
   - python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate || python -m venv .venv\
.venv\Scripts\activate (windows note)
   - pip install -e ./sdk[dev] --no-cache-dir
   - export REDWOOD_API_KEY=<dev_key> (or use .env.local)
   - make lint || ./scripts/lint.sh (use the team's linter presets)

2) Quick unit smoke (2 minutes)
   - pytest tests/smoke/test_smoke_minimal.py -q
   - Look for two things in failures: missing imports and network/timeouts.

3) Sampleapp run (3–5 minutes)
   - cd examples/minimal && ./run_local.sh
   - Confirm: sample responds to a prompt, streaming works, and cost estimate printed in logs

4) Telemetry handshake check (1 minute)
   - Ensure local telemetry ping appears in internal test dashboard (tag=first-commit/<username>)

The smoke-loop (pre-PR checklist):
- lint: pass (no new autofixable warnings)
- unit-smoke: tests/smoke/test_smoke_minimal.py OK
- sample-app: example/minimal demo runs end-to-end locally
- contract check: run ./scripts/verify_api_contract.sh (validates shapes used by examples)
- lightweight load: curl -sS http://localhost:8080/health && curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -d '{"prompt":"ping"}' (should return within 250ms locally in dev mode)
- docs sanity: docs/README.md updated if public surface changed

Observability + telemetry (practical):
- Emit a single lightweight event at first run: sdk.first_commit (tags: user, branch, sampleapp)
- Emit smoke-loop result: sdk.smoke_loop.result = pass|fail and sdk.smoke_loop.duration_ms
- Telemetry fields (minimum): environment (local|ci), sdk_version, git_sha_short, username
- If telemetry is disabled locally, print a clear warning and log a local-only trace file at ~/.redwood/sdk-first-commit.json for debugging

Quick commands cheat-sheet (copy/paste friendly):
- Setup: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/sdk.git && cd sdk && python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -e '.[dev]'
- Run smoke unit: pytest tests/smoke/test_smoke_minimal.py -q
- Start sampleapp: cd examples/minimal && REDWOOD_API_KEY=__mock__ ./run_local.sh
- Verify telemetry: scripts/check_telemetry.sh --tag first-commit/<you>

Failure modes we often hit (and quick fixes):
- Missing compiled extension: run scripts/build_wheels.sh and re-install editable install
- Network proxy/timeouts: set HTTP_PROXY for corp network or use --offline to run local emulator
- Linter differences across machines: run 'prettier --write' and ensure node/npm versions match .nvmrc
- Flaky sampleapp port collisions: ./run_local.sh uses PORT=${PORT:-8080} so try PORT=8081 ./run_local.sh

Review checklist (for PR reviewer):
- Does the PR change public SDK surface? If yes, must update examples and docs/README.md
- Are smoke-loop artifacts in place (scripts/verify_api_contract.sh, tests/smoke/*)?
- Can reviewer run smoke-loop in under 15 minutes? If not, ask for pruning steps or automation
- Are telemetry events minimal and privacy-safe? No PII.

Automation roadmap (next steps, not gate):
- Turn the manual smoke-loop into a single command: ./scripts/first_commit_check.sh --local --tag <user>
- Add ephemeral test dashboard view for first-commit pings (concourse/Grafana)
- Add a GitHub workflow that flags PRs that fail the smoke-loop and posts reproducible steps as a comment

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Should first-commit telemetry be opt-in? We currently log anonymous metrics; privacy team asked for opt-in for early-access builds.
- How strict should the smoke-loop be for small documentation PRs? (suggestion: bypass with PR label 'docs-only' + auto-run minimal checks)
- How to handle sampleapps that require cloud keys (we should provide hermetic mock emulators).

Immediate TODOs (small actionable items):
- [ ] Miguel: prototype ./scripts/first_commit_check.sh (P0, 2d)
- [ ] Rae: add telemetry tag propagation to examples/minimal (P1, 3d)
- [ ] Samir: add a health-check curl wrapper for developer machines (P1, 1d)
- [ ] Aisha: draft short onboarding blurb for new hires linking to this ritual (P0, 1d)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep ritual minimal and forgiving; it exists to unblock, not gate contributions.
- Make failures actionable: error messages should say exactly which step failed and one-line fix.
- If we add more gating, prefer optional strict mode (./first_commit_check.sh --strict)

References and inspiration:
- Small-team "first-run" rituals from infra-team (see RED-1022 retro notes)
- Example health-check patterns in serving-runtime repo (scripts/dev-health.sh)
- UX: onboarding survey we ran in 2024 (results in confluence link above)

If you're running this for the first time, ping #devx-onboarding in Slack and add a note to your PR: "ran first-commit ritual — smoke loop passed locally". That small signal helps maintainers triage faster.
